Field notes

What this world models

Each fly has an artificial recurrent neural controller. Two parents pass starting traits and network genes to offspring; acquired neural changes are not copied. Mutation may add or remove neurons and connections. A simple food-seeking reflex seeds the founders—it is not an evolved finding.

Model boundaries and full-connectome status

This running ecosystem does not use the 166,700-neuron biological fly connectome. Full-connectome data verification and a separate neural assay are provided with the project; population-scale integration is not active here. These are artificial life histories and simulation seconds, not biological days. Learning is a candidate reward-modulated rule, not established improved behavior.
